content:
leo: Heads up — seen a 12–18% p95/p99 tail regression on host-side for small requests since the kernel-selector rollout. Short sequences (<64) are worst affected. Flame/profile points to proto.decode -> tokenize -> kvcache.lookup -> net.writev path being hotter than before. Suspect an extra copy in the preparse shim.

leo: quick pprof snippet from the canary:```
pprof top
40.3%  proto.decode
25.1%  tokenization.Tokenize
12.7%  net.writev
8.2%   kvcache.Lookup
4.5%   preparse.NormalizeHeaders
3.0%   runtime.growslice
```

leo: reproducer we used: `tools/repro/mini-ingest-bench --small-reqs --qps 500 --seq-len 32`

marta: starting a bisect now across commits abc123..def456, will report numbers.

marta: early results — reverting change 9fb2a (preparse: normalize header bytes) drops p99 by ~12% in the harness. Patch added a `bytes.Copy` when normalizing which may be the extra allocation/copy.

marta: repro commands + perf capture:```
# run repro
./mini-ingest-bench --small-reqs --qps 500 --out /tmp/perf
# capture pprof
pprof -seconds 30 http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile > /tmp/perf/pprof.pb
```

ben: fyi I instrumented grpc/write path on the same canary — smallwrite calls spiked from ~200us to ~600us when compression + hpack is on. Looks like more small frames are being emitted after normalize.

ben: try enabling writev coalesce in the proxy to see if that mitigates: `--writev-coalesce=on` or flip `proxy.writev_coalesce=true` in config. That removed ~40% of net.writev time in my local run.

triage-bot: Created ticket RED-2025: "host-side small-request tail regression after kernel-selector change" assigned to eng-runtime, priority P2.

olivia: Can we prioritize for tomorrow's shiproom? Need a canary + rollback plan if this impacts Dedicated customers.

leo: Working on a small patch to remove the extra bytes.Copy in preparse; added microbench and unit test. Putting up PR now and will run canary against ingress traffic.

leo: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/894 (WIP) — includes benchmark numbers in description.

marta: landed a hotfix revert to a staging canary; early telemetry looks good — p99 back to baseline in staging after the revert.

ben: great. after revert I'll enable writev_coalesce in a controlled canary to shave net tail further.

olivia: schedule rollback window if PR doesn't land by EOD.

leo: thanks all — will follow up with final postmortem and measurement graphs. :thumbsup:
